title: Interlock Logic & Cause Effect Matrix - FA-8901 (SEQ-8901)
content:
INTERLOCK LOGIC & CAUSE EFFECT MATRIX: SEQ-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR (FA-8901) OVERHEAD PROTECTION LOGIC).
Document No: TJC-LLD-IL-FA-8901, Revision: Rev.03, Status: Issued for Operation, SIL Level: SIL 1.
Equipment: FA-8901, Functional Location: TJC-LLD-8900-01.
CAUSE & EFFECT MATRIX (TRIPS):
- T1: Drum level HIGH-HIGH (LSHH-8901 > 85 %, 1oo2) -> Actions: Trip Feed (EFF-1), DCS Alarm (EFF-4)
- T2: Drum level LOW-LOW (LSLL-8901 < 15 %, 1oo2) -> Actions: Trip Pump (EFF-2), DCS Alarm (EFF-4)
- T3: Drum pressure HIGH-HIGH (PSHH-8902 > 8 barg, 1oo2) -> Actions: Open Min-Flow (EFF-3), DCS Alarm (EFF-4)
- T4: Emergency stop (manual) (HS-8901 Manual, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip Feed (EFF-1), Trip Pump (EFF-2), Open Min-Flow (EFF-3), DCS Alarm (EFF-4)
START PERMISSIVES (AND-gate conditions to start):
- P1: Level in normal band (20-80%) (LT-8901, Gate: AND)
- P2: N2 blanket healthy (PT-8902, Gate: AND)
- P3: Boot not flooded (LT-8903, Gate: AND)
- P4: No active trip / reset done (DCS reset, Gate: AND)
- —: ALL permissives TRUE → START FA-8901 ENABLED (—, Gate: AND)
CROSS REFERENCES: P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-8901, Datasheet: TJC-LLD-DS-FA-8901.

title: One Point Lesson - Level Gauge / Bridle Verification (LT-8901) (OPL-FA-8901-01)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-FA-8901-01 - Level Gauge / Bridle Verification (LT-8901).

Equipment: FA-8901, Discipline: Instrument, Area: 8900 - HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: SEQ-8901 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-8901.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains level gauge / bridle verification (lt-8901) for FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM) in the HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM. A false level reading causes reflux pump cavitation (low) or column flooding (high); the transmitter must agree with the gauge. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Cross-check LT-8901 against the level bridle gauge
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Blow down the bridle to clear any plugging
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Confirm the LSHH-8901 and LSLL-8901 switch actions
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Verify the level tracks correctly through a level change
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Log any deviation and recalibrate if needed
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Reflux drum level transmitter drifting vs gauge | Cause: Transmitter zero drift | Action: Recalibrated LT-8901 against the bridle gauge
- Symptom: Blanket / vent split-range valve hunting | Cause: Split-range calibration overlap incorrect | Action: Re-tuned PCV-8905 split-range, verified PT-8902 hold
- Symptom: Proof test of drum high-high level trip | Cause: Within tolerance | Action: Recalibrated LSHH-8901 and verified EFF-1 column feed trip

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A false level reading causes reflux pump cavitation (low) or column flooding (high); the transmitter must agree with the gauge.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-8901: e.g. LSHH-8901 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
